concepts.name: Cinematic Chapters
concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Make one exquisitely art-directed, high-fidelity DESKTOP SERVICES PAGE mockup for ORBIT AERIALS, a Kuwait-based aerial construction documentation and spatial intelligence studio. Flat webpage screenshot, about 1536 x 1280, no device mockup, no browser frame, no external moodboard captions. This is an inner SERVICES page, not a generic landing page. Show enough page depth for a distinctive service navigation AND a second content section. Exact crisp readable English typesetting, excellent hierarchy, plausible buildable web design, polished details. Use the supplied brand image as the ONLY logo: preserve the six-petal orbital symbol, vertical divider, ORBIT AERIALS wordmark and tagline. Scale it to a realistic small header size. You may invert white to black on a light background. Do not invent a logo. Brand reference is for identity only, NOT for page layout.

All concepts share the same actual business content: 'Services', main proposition 'Your project. Every perspective.', and these FIVE service names: 'Progress documentation', 'Spatial mapping', '360° walkthroughs', 'Time-lapse', 'Handover films'. Short descriptor: 'Aerial capture, spatial intelligence and visual storytelling for the built world.' Header navigation: 'Services', 'About', 'Journal', 'Contact'; CTA 'Start a project'. Include a discreet 'Illustrative imagery' caption near the main image. No invented clients, portfolio projects, certifications, accuracy claims, testimonial quotes, success statistics, or live metrics. Realistic Gulf construction settings, not cartoon 3D toy buildings, drones as products, futuristic cities or sci-fi effects. Absolutely no generic three-card features grid. Treat the visual imagery as the service demonstration. 
DIRECTION 1 — CINEMATIC CHAPTERS. Rich near-black film-editor aesthetics with immersive aerial cinematography. The layout must feel like browsing a beautifully directed documentary, not a tech dashboard. Full-bleed bird's-eye photograph of a LARGE Gulf construction site in low warm morning light across the upper 75% of the page. Real cranes, slabs, excavators, complex earthworks, delicate dust and long geometric shadows. The photo is crisply REALISTIC with natural sandy colours, subdued, quietly dramatic, not orange-graded or hyperreal CGI. At top a slim transparent header with small white original logo left and understated white navigation right. Lower-left within the photo put a very large beautifully composed three-line LIGHT-WEIGHT sans-serif headline 'Your project.' / 'Every' / 'perspective.' occupying 42% width, graceful negative space, not chunky. The rest of photo remains visible. Right lower corner has a restrained 100px circular outlined play control with 'Watch a perspective' below.
The defining SERVICES NAVIGATION is a horizontal editing filmstrip spanning the page just under the main image, five unequal naturally sized chapter cells separated only by fine white ticks. Each has a tiny realistic thumbnail above the exact service label. Active first chapter is bright; others muted but readable. Above strip, tiny '01 / 05' and 'Explore our services'. No pill card boxes. On the near-black lower 25% below strip, reveal a deliberate asymmetric next section: small left label '01 / PROGRESS DOCUMENTATION', large middle headline 'Watch a place become.' and right-side compact descriptor 'A consistent visual record, from the first groundwork to the final handover.' plus small plain link 'Explore the service ↗'. Elegant dark film portfolio, spatial and image-rich. White type, warm images, tiny muted gold functional accent only. Distinctive photographic composition and refined pacing.

Include short service proposition in tiny dark body type in the upper whitespace. Entire design light, scholarly, premium, confident; bespoke scale and typographic rhythm.

DIRECTION 3 — SURVEY ROOM. A lush, deep forest-green spatial canvas with precise pale mint lines. An interactive geographical survey table. This should convey that the user is EXPLORING a construction site and its deliverables. Not generic sci-fi HUD, not analytics SaaS, not background wireframe behind normal landing copy. The information architecture IS the spatial explorer.
The entire page has dark evergreen #102A26 base. Header: original white logo scaled small left, small pale navigation and outline rectangular 'Start a project' right. Main page is arranged as an asymmetrical expedition atlas: a slim 290px LEFT contents rail, enormous main site map area to its right, and a compact bottom output legend. Leave all five names readable, wrap naturally. At bottom of rail a precise small 'Talk to Orbit ↗' link.
MAIN CANVAS: enormous highly detailed realistic oblique SURVEY reconstruction of a sprawling active construction district occupying 70% of the total page width and 75% height. Actual textured dusty buildings and earthworks at one side; dense mint/ivory point cloud and carefully drawn contour/structural lines on the other. Edge of survey irregular like a real drone scan, not rectangular plinth. Sophisticated layered spatial depth and authentic fine point texture. Add only THREE small meaningful hotspot labels with small pins, connected with precise hairlines: 'Progress documentation', '360° walkthroughs', 'Spatial mapping'; keep labels clear of site. Small functional segmented switch 'Photogrammetry / Point cloud / DSM' at top of map and a thin comparison slider at its bottom. NO invented coordinates, measurements, status widgets, target crosshairs, blinking signals or fake charts.
Below canvas, a large full-width olive-grey footer band: left tiny 'OUTPUTS', giant elegant 'One site. Many ways to see it.' in 45px light sans; right three compact image strips showing actual aerial texture, point cloud and elevation colour map, with their names. A very small 'Illustrative imagery' note. Luxurious engineering atlas, intriguing but legible, green throughout, restrained mint and pale yellow cues, precise all-sharp corners.

DIRECTION 4 — INDEX IN MOTION. A radical typographic service catalogue, like a world-class contemporary design studio with construction intelligence. Colour system: light cool-grey #E7E9E5 canvas, near-black #171C19 typography, vivid safety-orange #F05B35 used for ONE active service row and small markers. Flat ink, clean strong rules, NO gradients, NO neon, NO decorative grid backgrounds, NO pill buttons. Main layout must be TOTALLY different from an image hero or white model display. Typography and an enormous service index ARE the main interaction.
Header is a pale grey slim band with original black-inverted logo on the left, compact black 'Services / About / Journal / Contact' right and clean text CTA. Under header, a small upper kicker row: left 'Your project. Every perspective.', right small two-line descriptor about aerial capture and spatial intelligence. Then begin FIVE HUGE horizontal ruled service rows filling most of the page. Each service label is set in outstanding, tightly tracked, very large semi-condensed grotesk (70-100px), not serif. Tiny number 01–05 at far left and simple thin diagonal arrow far right. These are text rows, no boxed cards. All five exact service names must be visible with plausible spacing. Make the active SECOND row 'Spatial mapping' expanded to 400px tall with a safety-orange background. At left inside active row: huge black 'Spatial' then 'mapping', small 2-line copy 'Turn a site into spatial understanding.' and text action 'Explore mapping ↗'. At right inside this orange row: a SHARP rectangular 3:2 real aerial construction-site image with a vertical reveal division switching half of it into an authentic dense white point cloud on dark-charcoal background, around 540x300. Its image thumbnail intrudes slightly across the row boundary with deliberate orderly alignment. Small functional handle at reveal division, undercaption 'Drag to compare'. Make all type have refined line spacing and accurate alignment. Other four rows stay light grey with huge dark labels: 'Progress documentation', '360° walkthroughs', 'Time-lapse', 'Handover films'. Lower boundary has short small note 'Built to reveal the bigger picture.' and tiny black original orbital symbol. The memorable feeling is a kinetic index where hovering a service expands an image stage. Very graphic, confident and architectural, safety-orange is a purposeful construction reference, not a corporate generic accent. No made-up projects or numbers besides index numbers.
